data.ruling:
The refutation does not hold, and the RP2354B stays. The stock verifier confirmed every check. The datasheet verifier failed two checks. Neither one is a property of the part that fails this function.

(1) 'watchdog window (V1 and V2)', passes false. The silicon sets any watchdog timeout from 0 to 0xffffff us, about 16.8 s (Table 1249). That range meets each bound on its own: a timeout at or below 200 ms (V1) and a timeout above 900 ms (V2). The window is empty only because the two values found for research contradict each other. V1 is 200 ms, read from IOBoard.md:186 and link_dev.h. V2 is 900 ms: a 400 ms packaged-part sector erase plus a 500 ms blocking USB console write. The 400 ms erase alone is already above 200 ms. No watchdog on any microcontroller can meet both values, so the conflict cannot count against this part. The verifier says the same ('not a defect of the part'). It is also a fixed input. Research.md Scope says a fixed input is checked for stock, lifecycle and a second source, and a failed check goes to the owner rather than to re-selection. All three of those checks pass. The same ruling was made in T2 (adjudicator-R1, 2026-09-28). The conflict still goes to the owner and to P5 as a finding: Q8 (moving the store off the flash) and the console timeout both change V2. The verifier also says V1 is refuted as not found. No 'found V1' check is among the failed checks given to this adjudicator. That question bears on the owner's conflict, not on the part.

(2) 'GPIO reset state', agrees false but passes true. I re-read the verifier's claim and it holds: the record's statement was wrong. Section 9.7 says the isolation latches reset only on POR, BOR, RUN, CDBGRSTREQ and rescue reset. The same section also says 'resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state'. Section 12.9.4 lets the watchdog run a PSM sequence through PSM_WDSEL, and Table 532 bit 4 of PSM_WDSEL is RESETS. In the RESETS RESET register (Table 535), PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) reset to 0x1, which holds them in reset. pico-sdk 2.3.0 _watchdog_enable() sets PSM_WDSEL to every bit except ROSC and XOSC (watchdog.c:53). So a watchdog reset set up that way returns the in-use Bank 0 pads to their reset state. Pads never used stay isolated in their power-up state. That is what IOBoard.md:221 needs ('every gate the coprocessor drives opens while its pins are at their reset state'). The disagreement is in the part's favour: the record understated the part. The part meets the requirement. The corrected figure goes to the owner and to R4 and R6 in place of the record's 'not shown'. One case remains not shown: a watchdog reset configured only at the switched-core or POWMAN level. The image enables no watchdog at all yet (V4: firmware/iomcu/ has only the comment at main.c:970-973).

Neither finding concerns lifecycle, an end-of-life notice, the maker allowlist or the LCSC identity. Both concern this function's requirement values, so the scope is function.

- Section 12.9.4: 'PSM_WDSEL allows the watchdog to trigger system resets by running a full or partial PSM sequence'; 'RESETS_WDSEL allows the watchdog to trigger subsystem resets'.
- Table 532, PSM WDSEL: bit 4 RESETS, bit 3 XOSC, bits 24:0 RW, reset 0x0.
- Table 535, RESETS RESET: bit 9 PADS_BANK0 reset 0x1; bit 6 IO_BANK0 reset 0x1.
- Section 9.7: 'The isolation latches themselves are reset by ... Power-on reset, Brownout reset, RUN pin being asserted low, SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ, RP-AP rescue reset'; 'The ISO control bits are not reset by the PADS register block reset driven by the RESETS control registers: resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads'. The same section: 'The SDK automatically clears the ISO bit when gpio_set_function() is called'.
